paragraphs: Universal Insurance Holdings, Inc. ("UVE," and together with its wholly-owned subsidiaries, "we," "our," "us," or the "Company") is a holding company offering property and casualty insurance and value-added insurance services. We develop, market, and underwrite insurance products for consumers predominantly in the personal residential homeowners lines of business and perform substantially all other insurance-related services for our primary insurance entities, including risk management, claims management, and distribution. Our primary insurance entities, Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company ("UPCIC") and American Platinum Property and Casualty Insurance Company ("APPCIC" and together with UPCIC, the "Insurance Entities"), offer insurance products through both our appointed independent agent network and our online distribution channels across our multi-state footprint (primarily in Florida). The Insurance Entities seek to produce an underwriting profit (defined as earned premium minus losses, loss adjustment expense ("LAE"), policy acquisition costs and other operating costs and expenses) over the long term; maintain a conservative balance sheet to prepare for years in which the Insurance Entities are not able to achieve an underwriting profit; and generate investment income on assets.

UVE's strategic focus is on creating a best-in-class experience for our customers and delivering strong shareholder returns across underwriting cycles. While weather-related volatility is an inherent part of property insurance, particularly in coastal markets such as Florida, our strategy includes generating non-risk bearing income that enhances returns in profitable underwriting periods, while serving as a buffer and potentially still allowing for consolidated profitability in challenging underwriting periods. We have more than 25 years of experience providing protection solutions. We continue to focus on disciplined underwriting in opportune markets and maintaining a resilient balance sheet that is enhanced by our reinsurance program. We have made substantial efforts in recent years to innovate across all of our service businesses, including continued development of our digital agency Clovered.com, where we have 39 carrier partners, and utilization of digital applications where applicable to administer claims. We continue to evaluate ways in which we can improve the customer experience across all touchpoints of the insurance value chain.

UPCIC, our primary risk-bearing insurance entity, which accounts for the substantial majority of our Insurance Entities' business, primarily distributes policies through our independent agency network and offers the following types of personal residential insurance: homeowners, renters/tenants, condo unit owners, and dwelling/fire. UPCIC also offers allied lines, coverage for other structures, and personal property, liability, and personal articles coverages. APPCIC writes similar lines of insurance as UPCIC, but is only licensed in Florida and Georgia. APPCIC primarily distributes policies through our digital platforms, and beginning in the current year through our independent agency network.

Our Insurance Entities, UPCIC and APPCIC, are both currently rated "A" ("Exceptional") by Demotech, Inc. ("Demotech") and "A-" by Kroll Bond Rating Agency ("Kroll"), which are rating agencies specializing in evaluating insurer financial strength and stability. Our combined statutory capital and surplus was approximately $509.1 million at December 31, 2025.

Our subsidiary, Evolution Risk Advisors, Inc. ("ERA," formerly Universal Risk Advisors, Inc.), is the managing general agent for the Insurance Entities. In this capacity, ERA advises on actuarial issues, oversees distribution, administers claims payments, performs policy administration and underwriting, and assists with reinsurance negotiations. ERA's underwriting service evaluates insurance risk and exposures on an individual and portfolio basis and assists the Insurance Entities with pricing risks. All underwriting is performed utilizing our state-filed rate and rule manuals as the basis of our rate-making and risk assessment. ERA collects fees from the Insurance Entities for the services it provides, as well as certain policy fees from insureds. Our subsidiary, Universal Inspection Corporation d/b/a Wicklow Inspection Corporation, complements ERA and our Insurance Entities by conducting inspections as part of our underwriting process.

The Insurance Entities rely heavily on reinsurance to limit potential exposure to catastrophic events. In most years, reinsurance coverage is one of the most significant costs we incur. In conjunction with ERA, our licensed reinsurance intermediary, Blue Atlantic Reinsurance Corporation ("BARC"), partners with a third-party reinsurance broker to place and manage our reinsurance programs for the Insurance Entities. BARC receives commission revenue, net of third-party co-broker fees, from third-party reinsurers in connection with these services, which can serve to mitigate reinsurance costs.

Due to our exposure to Florida's residential property insurance market, we face risks associated with the adverse conditions that have affected the magnitude of both catastrophe and non-catastrophe losses and LAE in Florida in recent years. Although the Florida legislature passed law changes to address market abuses, including substantial reforms in December 2022, the benefits of these law changes may not be fully realized for several years while the Company continues to settle and respond to claims that occurred prior to reforms taking full effect. We have sought, and continue to seek, to mitigate these risks through our exposure management initiatives, efforts to attain rate adequacy, implementing product updates, and tailoring our claims and legal processes to market conditions.

As we are a property and casualty insurance company with a concentration in Florida and other coastal states, natural catastrophes are among the most serious risks facing our customers and communities. Changing climate conditions are increasing the unpredictability of natural catastrophes, such as hurricanes, floods, severe convective storms, and wildfires, leading to significant property losses. Our responsive claims team helps to restore our customers' lives after catastrophic losses. Our enterprise risk management framework, overseen by senior management and the Board of Directors (the "Board of Directors" or the "Board"), models and assesses loss probabilities. We seek to mitigate catastrophe risk for our customers and shareholders through prudent exposure management, underwriting initiatives, and sensitivity to geographic concentrations as well as through reinsurance as noted above.

Our subsidiary, Universal Adjusting Corporation d/b/a Alder Adjusting ("Alder"), manages our claims processing and adjusting functions from claim inception to conclusion, which we believe allows us to increase efficiency and provide a high level of customer service. Alder updates its claims-handling procedures over time in response to market trends. Through Alder, we have adopted initiatives to adjust and pay straightforward, meritorious claims as promptly as possible through timely analysis and on-site field adjusting. Alder also has increased its use of technology to inspect properties and facilitate adjusting claims. In addition to our in-house claims operation, we assign some field inspections to third-party adjusters. Our relationships with these adjusters enable us to continue to provide high quality and timely service following a catastrophe, such as a hurricane in coastal states, and during any other period of unusually high claim volume. Through our continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives, we continue to evaluate ways in which we can improve the customer's claims experience. Alder's data intelligence allows the Insurance Entities, ERA, and our reinsurance partners to identify trends and refine the underwriting process and guidelines to seek adequate pricing and identify needed adjustments. Our claims management operations provide cost-effective solutions in servicing claims for the Insurance Entities and generates additional fee income from adjusting claims ceded to reinsurers.

Our in-house claims litigation team continues to focus on more effectively and efficiently protecting our rights in litigation, including through subrogation. Subrogation is the act of seeking reimbursement from a third party that caused a covered event to an insured for the amount we paid on the insured's behalf. Reflecting our efforts to improve and enhance our claims operations and to address emerging claims and litigation trends, approximately 54% of our employees work in our claims management operations. Of these employees, 56% comprise our in-house claims litigation team.

We market and sell our products primarily through our network of approximately 9,500 licensed independent agents (3,900 in Florida). Our strong relationships with our independent agents and their relationships with their customers are critical to our ability to identify, attract, and retain profitable business. We actively participate in the recruitment and training of our independent agents and provide each agency with training sessions on topics such as underwriting guidelines and submitting claims.

We utilize an attractive commission-based compensation plan as an incentive for independent agents to place business with us. We also strive to provide excellent service to our independent agents and brokers, which has yielded long-standing partnerships with our independent agents (a number of which have relationships with us that span more than a decade) that benefit the Company in our target markets through hard and soft market cycles. Our internal staff and specialists support our independent agents by providing access to our in-house technology systems to assist with the delivery of service to our policyholders. This arrangement creates a collaborative environment between the Company and our independent agents on continuous improvement initiatives and allows our independent agents to provide quotes within minutes. Our technology systems have evolved into a highly valued tool that enables agents to quickly understand the status of a policy and assist their clients with policy-related questions.

In addition to distributing our products through our independent agency network, we offer direct-to-consumer online distribution, including through our wholly-owned digital insurance agency, Clovered, which is operational across our multi-state footprint. As a personal lines property and casualty insurance agency, Clovered also partners with third-party insurance carriers and offers a wide suite of property and casualty insurance products, allowing us to earn non-risk bearing commission revenue for placing insurance on their behalf.

Funds in excess of operating needs for the Insurance Entities and UVE are invested in accordance with our investment policy guidelines. The Investment Committee of our Board oversees the investment portfolio and reports overall investment results to our Board, on a quarterly basis. The investment activities of the Insurance Entities are subject to regulation and supervision by the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation ("FLOIR"). See below under "—Government Regulation." The Insurance Entities may only make investments that are consistent with regulatory guidelines, and our more restrictive investment policy guidelines for the Insurance Entities, including but not limited to, credit quality and concentration thresholds by issuer, by security type, and in aggregate, an average duration cap, and quarterly realized loss budget requirements. The primary objectives of our investment portfolio are the preservation of capital and providing adequate liquidity for claims payments and other cash needs. The portfolio's secondary investment objective is to generate a stable risk-commensurate return with an emphasis on investment income while at the same time maintaining the high-quality standards of the portfolio. Our investment guidelines for fixed-income investments limit duration to 5 years or less and require a portfolio average credit rating of A- or better. UVE is not subject to the statutory investment guidelines governing insurance companies. Therefore, the investments made by UVE may differ from those made by the Insurance Entities.

headings: Because we have significant exposure to the Florida market, our financial results are affected by the regulatory, economic and weather conditions in Florida.
We have entered new markets and expect that we will continue to do so, but there can be no assurance that our diversification and growth strategy will be effective.
Actual claims incurred have exceeded, and in the future may exceed, reserves established for claims, adversely affecting our operating results and financial condition.
Unanticipated increases in the severity or frequency of claims adversely affect our profitability and financial condition.
The failure of the risk mitigation strategies we utilize could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.
Pandemics and macroeconomic conditions could impact our business, financial results and growth.
We rely on models as a tool to evaluate risk, and those models are inherently uncertain and may not accurately predict existing or future losses.
Reinsurance may be unavailable in the future at reasonable levels and prices or on reasonable terms, which may limit our ability to write new business or to adequately mitigate our exposure to loss.
Reinsurance subjects us to the credit risk of our reinsurers, which could have a material adverse effect on our operating results and financial condition.
Our financial condition and operating results are subject to the cyclical nature of the property and casualty insurance business.
An overall decline in the housing market or general economic conditions could have a material adverse effect on the financial condition and results of operations of our business.
Our success depends, in part, on our ability to attract, retain, and develop talented employees, and the loss of any one of our key personnel could adversely impact our operations.
We could be adversely affected if our controls designed to ensure compliance with guidelines, policies and legal and regulatory standards are not effective.
The failure of our claims professionals to effectively manage claims could adversely affect our insurance business and financial results.
Litigation or regulatory actions could result in material settlements, judgments, fines, or penalties and consequently have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and reputation.
Failure to maintain or enhance our brand or damage to our reputation could adversely impact our business.
Our future results are dependent in part on our ability to successfully operate in a highly competitive insurance industry.

A downgrade in our financial strength or stability ratings may have an adverse effect on our competitive position, the marketability of our product offerings, and our liquidity, operating results and financial condition.
Breaches or other failures of our information systems or denial of service on our website could have an adverse impact on our business and reputation.
We are subject to market risk, which may adversely affect investment income.
Our overall financial performance depends in part on the returns on our investment portfolio.
We are subject to extensive regulation, and potential further restrictive regulation may increase our operating costs and limit our growth and profitability.
paragraphs: The following summarizes the material factors that may render an investment in our securities speculative or risky. When any one or more of the following risks materialize from time to time, our business, reputation, financial condition, cash flows, and results of operations can be materially and adversely affected, and the trading price of our common stock could decline. These risk factors do not identify all risks that we face; our operations can also be affected by factors that are not presently known to us or that we currently consider to be immaterial to our operations, or by various risks that are generally applicable to most companies. Due to risks and uncertainties, known and unknown, our past financial results may not be a reliable indicator of future performance, and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods. Some of the factors, events, and contingencies described below have already affected us and may impact us again in the future.
RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND OPERATIONS

As a property and casualty insurer, we may face significant losses, and our financial results may vary from period to period, due to exposure to catastrophic events and severe weather conditions, the frequency and severity of which are affected by climate change.

Because of the exposure of our property and casualty business to catastrophic events, our operating results and financial condition have varied significantly from one period to the next, and our historical results of operations may not be indicative of future results of operations. Property damage resulting from catastrophes is the greatest risk of loss we face in the ordinary course of our business. Catastrophes can be caused by various natural disasters, including but not limited to hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes, tropical storms, sinkholes, windstorms, hailstorms, severe winter weather, and earthquakes. The frequency and severity of property insurance claims generally increase when catastrophic events and severe weather conditions occur.

Over the years, notable changes in long-term weather patterns have been observed, including an increase in both the frequency and intensity of severe convective events. These trends are frequently associated with climate change, a process linked to rising global temperatures that impact worldwide weather systems. In general, climate change may affect the occurrence of certain natural events, such as increasing the frequency or severity of wind, tornado, hailstorm, and thunderstorm events due to increased convection in the atmosphere. There could also be increasingly frequent wildfires in certain geographies, more flooding, and increased severity of hurricanes due to higher sea surface temperatures. To the extent the frequency or severity of weather events continues to be exacerbated due to changing weather patterns or conditions, we may experience increased catastrophe losses in both coastal and non-coastal areas. This may cause increases in claims-related and/or reinsurance costs and may negatively affect our ability to provide homeowners insurance to our policyholders in the future. In addition, increased frequency of catastrophic events could result in increased credit exposure to the reinsurers with which we transact business. Our actual losses from catastrophic events might exceed levels protected against by the Insurance Entities' respective reinsurance programs or might be larger than anticipated if one or more of our reinsurers fail to meet their obligations. As a result, incurred losses from such events and the demand, price and availability of reinsurance coverages for homeowners insurance may be affected.

In addition, despite our catastrophe management programs, we retain material exposure to catastrophic events. Our liquidity could be constrained by a catastrophe, or multiple catastrophes, which could have a negative impact on our business. Catastrophes have eroded, and in the future may erode, our statutory surplus or ability to obtain adequate reinsurance which could negatively affect our ability to write new or renewal business. Catastrophic claim severity is also impacted by the effects of continued, high levels of inflation and increases in insured value and factors such as the overall claims, legal and litigation environments in affected areas, in addition to the geographic concentration of insured property.

paragraphs: In 2024, for Florida, UPCIC implemented new homeowners policy rates, resulting in an average rate decrease of 1.5% compared to previous rates, effective for new policies August 15, 2024 and renewal policies May 17, 2025. These Florida rate changes were implemented under use and file rating laws and subsequently received regulatory approval. In October 2025, UPCIC implemented new homeowners policy rates for new and renewal business policies, resulting in an average rate decrease of 5.1% compared to previous rates with an effective date of October 16, 2025.

paragraphs: Universal Insurance Holdings, Inc. ("UVE," and together with its wholly-owned subsidiaries, "we," "our," "us," or the "Company") 是一家持有公司，提供財產與責任保險及附加價值保險服務。我們開發、行銷及承保保險產品，主要針對個人住宅屋主業務的消費者，並為我們的主要保險實體執行幾乎所有其他保險相關服務，包括風險管理、理賠管理及分銷。我們的主要保險實體，Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Company ("UPCIC") 和 American Platinum Property and Casualty Insurance Company ("APPCIC" and together with UPCIC, the "Insurance Entities")，透過我們的任命獨立經紀網路及線上分銷渠道，在我們的多州營運範圍（主要在佛羅裏達州）提供保險產品。Insurance Entities 的目標是長期產生承保獲利（定義為已收 premiums 減去損失、理賠費用（"LAE"）、保單取得成本及其他營運成本與費用）；維持保守的資產負債表，以應對 Insurance Entities 未能產生承保獲利的年份；並在資產上產生投資收入。

UVE 的戰略重點在於為客戶創造最佳等級的體驗，並在承保週期中為股東創造強勁回報。雖然天氣相關的波動是財產保險的內在部分，特別是在佛羅裏達州等沿岸市場，我們的策略包括產生非風險性收入，以增強在獲利承保週期中的回報，同時作為緩衝，並可能在挑戰性的承保週期中仍能實現整體獲利。我們有超過 25 年的經驗提供保護解決方案。我們持續專注於在合適市場進行嚴謹的承保，並維持一個強韌的資產負債表，這由我們的再保險計劃所強化。我們在近年來持續努力創新所有服務業務，包括持續發展我們的數位經紀 Clovered.com，我們有 39 個電信業者夥伴，並在適用場合使用數位應用程式來處理理賠。我們持續評估如何改善客戶體驗，以提升保險價值鏈的所有接觸點。

UPCIC 是我們的主要風險承擔保險實體，佔我們 Insurance Entities 業務的絕大多數，主要透過我們的獨立經紀網路分銷保單，並提供以下類型的個人住宅保險：屋主、租客/租戶、公寓單位所有者及住宅/火災。UPCIC 也提供相關業務，其他結構的覆蓋，以及個人財產、責任及個人物品的覆蓋。APPCIC 提供與 UPCIC 相似的保險業務，但僅在佛羅裏達州和喬治亞州有執照。APPCIC 主要透過我們的數位平台分銷保單，並從本年度開始透過我們的獨立經紀網路分銷。

我們的 Insurance Entities，UPCIC 和 APPCIC，目前均由 Demotech, Inc. ("Demotech") 評為 "A" ("Exceptional")，並由 Kroll Bond Rating Agency ("Kroll") 評為 "A-"，這些是專門評估保險公司財務強度與穩定性的評級機構。我們的合併法定資本與準備金在 2025 年 12 月 31 日約為 509.1 百萬美元。

我們的子公司 Evolution Risk Advisors, Inc. ("ERA," 原為 Universal Risk Advisors, Inc.) 是 Insurance Entities 的管理總經紀。在此角色中，ERA 建議會計問題，監督分銷，處理理賠付款，執行保單行政與承保，並協助再保險談判。ERA 的承保服務評估保險風險與暴露，個別及整體 portfolio 基礎，並協助 Insurance Entities 進行風險定價。所有承保均使用我們州內提交的費率與規則手冊作為我們費率制定與風險評估的基礎。ERA 從 Insurance Entities 收取服務費用，以及某些保單費用從被保險人收取。我們的子公司 Universal Inspection Corporation d/b/a Wicklow Inspection Corporation，透過執行我們的承保程序中的檢查，補足 ERA 與我們的 Insurance Entities。

Insurance Entities 依賴再保險來限制潛在的災難性事件暴露。在大多數年份，再保險覆蓋是我們最重大的成本之一。與 ERA 合作，我們的經許可再保險中介 Blue Atlantic Reinsurance Corporation ("BARC")，與第三方再保險經紀合作，為 Insurance Entities 處理與管理再保險計劃。BARC 從第三方再保險公司收取佣金收入，扣除第三方共經紀費用，這些服務可以有助於降低再保險成本。

由於我們在佛羅裏達州住宅財產保險市場的暴露，我們面臨與近期年份中影響災難與非災難損失及 LAE 酬金規模的惡劣條件相關的風險。雖然佛羅裏達州立法機構已通過法律變更來解決市場濫用問題，包括 2022 年 12 月的重大改革，但這些法律變更的效益可能需要數年才能完全實現，而公司持續處理並回應改革生效前的理賠。我們已尋求，並持續尋求，透過我們的暴露管理計畫、努力達成適當的費率、實施產品更新，以及根據市場條件調整我們的理賠與法律程序，來緩解這些風險。

由於我們是一家專注於佛羅裏達州及其他沿岸州的財產與責任保險公司，自然災難是我們客戶與社區面臨的最嚴重風險之一。氣候條件的變化正在增加自然災難的不可預測性，例如颶風、洪水、強對流天氣及野火，導致重大財產損失。我們的應變理賠團隊協助客戶在災難性損失後恢復生活。我們的企業風險管理架構，由高層管理及董事會（"董事會"或"董事會"）監督，模擬並評估損失機率。我們透過謹慎的暴露管理、承保計畫及對地理集中度的敏感度，以及透過再保險如上所述，來緩解對客戶與股東的災難風險。

本公司之子公司 Universal Adjusting Corporation d/b/a Alder Adjusting ("Alder"), 負責我們從聲請開始至結案之聲請處理與調整功能，我們認為此安排可提高效率並提供高水準之客戶服務。Alder 會根據市場趨勢，持續更新其聲請處理程序。透過 Alder，我們已推行計畫，以盡可能迅速處理並支付簡單且具爭議性之聲請，透過及時分析與現場調整。Alder 亦增加使用科技來檢查財產並協助處理聲請。除本公司內部之聲請作業外，我們亦將部分現場檢查委由第三方調整者執行。我們與這些調整者之關係，使我們在如沿岸州之颶風等災難後，或任何聲請量異常高之期間，仍能持續提供高品質且及時之服務。透過我們持續改善與作業卓越之計畫，我們持續評估可改善客戶聲請經驗之方法。Alder 之數據智能使保險機構、ERA 及我們之再保險夥伴得以識別趨勢並改善承保流程與指引，以尋求適當之價格並識別所需之調整。我們之聲請管理作業為保險機構提供成本效益之聲請服務，並從轉讓給再保險機構之聲請中產生額外費用收入。
本公司內部之聲請訴訟團隊持續著重於更有效率地保護我們在訴訟中之權利，包括透過追償。追償係指向造成保險事件之第三方請求賠償，以償還我們為被保險人所支付之金額。反映我們改善與提升聲請作業之努力，以及應對新興聲請與訴訟趨勢，約 54% 之本公司員工從事聲請管理作業。這些員工中，56% 為本公司內部聲請訴訟團隊。
我們主要透過約 9,500 家經許可之獨立經紀人網路（佛羅裏達州為 3,900 家）來行銷與銷售我們之產品。我們與獨立經紀人及其與客戶之關係，對我們識別、吸引與留住獲利性業務至關重要。我們積極參與獨立經紀人之招募與培訓，並為每家經紀人提供培訓課程，主題包括承保指引與聲請提交等。

我們使用具有吸引力之佣金制薪資計畫，作為鼓勵獨立經紀人與我們合作之激勵措施。我們亦致力於提供優良服務予獨立經紀人與經紀，此舉已產生與我們獨立經紀人之長期合作關係（其中一些與我們之合作關係已逾十年），使本公司在目標市場中於硬市場與軟市場週期中均受益。本公司內部員工與專員透過提供對本公司內部科技系統之存取，協助經紀人提供對保單持有人之服務。此安排在本公司與獨立經紀人之間創造協作環境，使經紀人能於分鐘內提供報價。本公司之科技系統已發展成為高度受重視之工具，使經紀人能迅速瞭解保單狀態並協助客戶處理保單相關問題。
除透過獨立經紀人網路分銷我們之產品外，我們亦提供直接對消費者之線上分銷，包括透過我們全資擁有之數位保險經紀 Clovered，該經紀已在本公司多州營運範圍內運作。作為個人業務財產與責任保險經紀，Clovered 亦與第三方保險電信業者合作，並提供廣泛之財產與責任保險產品，使我們能為其代辦保險而賺取非風險性佣金收入。

保險機構與 UVE 之資金，超出營運需求者，依我們之投資政策指引進行投資。本公司董事會之投資委員會監督投資組合，並每季向董事會報告整體投資成果。保險機構之投資活動受佛羅裏達州保險監理處（"FLOIR"）之監管與監督。請參閱下文之 "—政府監管"。保險機構僅能進行符合監管指引之投資，且我們對保險機構之投資政策指引更為嚴格，包括但不限於發行者、證券類型及總體之信用品質與集中度門檻，以及平均存續期上限，及每季實現損失預算要求。我們投資組合之主要目標為資本之保存，並提供足夠流動性以應付聲請付款及其他現金需求。投資組合之次要目標為產生穩定且與風險相當之回報，同時維持投資組合之高品質標準。我們對固定收益投資之投資指引限制存續期為 5 年或以下，並要求投資組合平均信用評級為 A- 或以上。UVE 不受規範保險公司之法定投資指引所限制。因此，UVE 之投資可能與保險機構之投資不同。

headings: 因為我們在佛羅裏達州市場有重大 exposures，因此我們的財務結果會受到佛羅裏達州法規、經濟及天氣條件的影響。
我們已進入新市場，並預期將持續進行，但無法保證我們的多元化與成長策略會有效。
實際發生的索賠金額已超過，且未來可能超過所建立的索賠備抵，不利於我們的營運結果與財務狀況。
未預期的索賠嚴重程度或發生頻率增加，會對我們的獲利能力與財務狀況產生負面影響。
我們所使用的風險緩衝策略若失敗，可能會對我們的財務狀況或營運結果產生重大負面影響。
疫情與總體經濟條件可能影響我們的業務、財務結果與成長。
我們依賴模型作為評估風險的工具，而這些模型本質上具有不確定性，可能無法準確預測現有或未來的損失。
未來再保險可能無法在合理水平與價格或合理條件下取得，這可能會限制我們寫入新業務或充分緩衝我們損失風險的能力。
再保險使本公司面臨再保險公司的信用風險，此風險可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司財務狀況與營運成果受財產與意外保險業務週期性特質影響。
整體住宅市場或總體經濟條件下滑，可能對本公司業務的財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。
本公司成功在一定程度上取決於吸引、留住並培養優秀人才的能力，若任何一位關鍵人員離職，可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。
若本公司為確保符合指引、政策及法律與監管標準而設計的控制措施未能有效運作，可能對本公司造成不利影響。
若本公司理賠專業人員未能有效管理理賠，可能對本公司保險業務與財務結果造成不利影響。
訴訟或監管行動可能導致重大賠償、判決、罰款或處罰，進而對本公司財務狀況與聲譽造成重大不利影響。
未能維持或提升本公司品牌或聲譽受損，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司未來之績效部分取決於能否成功運作於高度競爭之保險產業。
若本公司財務強度或穩定性評級遭降級，可能對本公司之競爭地位、產品銷售能力、流動性、營運成果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
本公司資訊系統遭入侵或發生故障，或網站遭拒絕服務，可能對本公司之營運與聲譽產生負面影響。
本公司面臨市場風險，該風險可能對投資收益產生負面影響。
本公司整體財務表現部分取決於投資組合之回報率。
本公司受廣泛規範，潛在進一步限制性規範可能提高本公司營運成本，並限制本公司之成長與獲利能力。
paragraphs: 下列內容總結了可能使投資本公司證券成為投機性或風險性因素的重要事項。當任何一個或數個下列風險時而發生時，可能對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、現金流及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響，並可能導致本公司普通股的交易價格下跌。這些風險因素並未涵蓋本公司所面臨的所有風險；本公司營運也可能受到目前未知或本公司認為對營運不具重大影響的因素，或普遍適用於大多數公司的各種風險所影響。由於存在風險與不確定性，已知或未知的因素，本公司過去的財務表現可能無法作為未來表現的可靠指標，歷史趨勢也不應用來預測未來期間的結果或趨勢。
與本公司業務及營運相關的風險
作為財產與責任保險公司，我們可能面臨重大損失，且財務表現可能因遭受災難性事件及嚴峻天氣條件而有所波動，而這些事件的頻率與嚴重程度受氣候變遷影響。
由於財產與責任業務對災難性事件的暴露，我們的營運成果與財務狀況在不同期間間有顯著變動，我們的歷史營運成果可能無法反映未來的營運成果。財產損壞因災難所導致的損失，是我們在日常營運中所面臨的最大損失風險。災難可能由各種自然災害造成，包括但不限於颶風、野火、龍捲風、熱帶氣旋、地面塌陷、風暴、冰雹、嚴峻冬季天氣及地震。當災難性事件及嚴峻天氣條件發生時，財產保險索賠的頻率與嚴重程度通常會增加。

多年來，已觀察到長期天氣模式的顯著變化，包括嚴重對流事件的頻率與強度增加。這些趨勢通常與氣候變遷有關，氣候變遷是一種與全球溫度上升相關的過程，影響全球天氣系統。總體而言，氣候變遷可能影響某些自然事件的發生，例如因大氣中對流增加而提高風暴、龍捲風、冰雹及雷暴事件的頻率或嚴重程度。此外，某些地區也可能出現更頻繁的野火，更多淹水，以及因海水溫度升高而導致颶風的嚴重程度增加。若氣候變遷導致天氣事件的頻率或嚴重程度持續惡化，我們可能在沿海與非沿海地區都面臨增加的災難性損失。這可能會導致索賠相關及/或再保險成本增加，並可能影響我們未來為保單持有人提供住宅保險的能力。此外，災難性事件頻率增加可能導致我們與再保險公司交易時的信用風險增加。我們實際因災難性事件所產生的損失，可能超出再保險機構各自再保險計劃所保護的範圍，或若一個或多個再保險公司未能履行其義務，可能高於預期。因此，因這些事件所產生的損失及住宅保險再保險覆蓋的 demand、價格與可取得性可能受到影響。
此外，儘管我們有災難管理方案，我們仍對災難性事件保留重大風險敞口。災難可能限制我們的流動性，或多重災難可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。災難可能削減，且未來可能進一步削減，我們的法定準備金或取得足夠再保險的能力，這可能對我們寫新保單或續保業務的能力產生負面影響。災難性索賠的嚴重程度也受到持續高通貨膨脹、被保險價值增加以及整體索賠、法律與訴訟環境在受影響地區，以及被保險財產地理集中度等因素的影響。
